partners.mechanism_chain: GP1BA (HGNC:4439) —DISRUPTS→ GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155); GP1BB (HGNC:4440) —DISRUPTS→ GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155); GP9 (HGNC:4442) —DISRUPTS→ GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155); GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001873); GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal platelet aggregation (HP:0011285); GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding tendency (HP:0011407). Mutations in GP1BA, GP1BB, or GP9 disrupt the assembly and function of the GPIb-IX-V complex, a critical receptor on platelets involved in adhesion to von Willebrand factor and subsequent aggregation. ### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Bernard-Soulier syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.780)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-75892, Reactome:R-HSA-9769739, Reactome:R-HSA-9769743, Reactome:R-HSA-430116, Reactome:R-HSA-76009)

**Proposed mechanism:** GP1BA (HGNC:4439) —DISRUPTS→ GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155); GP1BB (HGNC:4440) —DISRUPTS→ GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155); GP9 (HGNC:4442) —DISRUPTS→ GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155); GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001873); GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal platelet aggregation (HP:0011285); GPIb-IX-V complex assembly and function (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding tendency (HP:0011407). Mutations in GP1BA, GP1BB, or GP9 disrupt the assembly and function of the GPIb-IX-V complex, a critical receptor on platelets involved in adhesion to von Willebrand factor and subsequent aggregation. This disruption leads to reduced platelet count (thrombocytopenia), impaired platelet aggregation, and a consequent bleeding tendency, manifesting as both platelet-type von Willebrand disease and Bernard-Soulier syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of functional variants in GP1BA, GP1BB, or GP9 that result in gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects, or variants in entirely different genes that are the sole cause of either disease, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: A common variant (allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) in GP1BA, GP1BB, or GP9 that is strongly associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of GPIb-IX-V complex dysfunction provides a basis for developing targeted therapies for bleeding disorders associated with platelet dysfunction, potentially including strategies to enhance platelet adhesion or aggregation.

#### 2. Bernard-Soulier syndrome, type A2, autosomal dominant  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.728)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-75892, Reactome:R-HSA-9769739, Reactome:R-HSA-9769743, Reactome:R-HSA-430116, Reactome:R-HSA-76009)

Mutations in GP1BA lead to a dysfunctional GPIb-IX-V complex, impairing von Willebrand factor binding and subsequent platelet adhesion, aggregation, and survival, manifesting as bleeding phenotypes and thrombocytopenia.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in GP1BA with a clear gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in either disease, or evidence of significant genetic contributions from other genes not involved in the GPIb-IX-V complex. _(variant: rs121917915)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis of these two related platelet disorders highlights the critical role of the GPIb-IX-V complex in hemostasis. Therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring the function of this complex or mitigating the downstream consequences of its dysfunction could potentially benefit patients with either condition.
